page: Amazon Web Services g6f.xlarge is a graphics-intensive virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical AMD EPYC 7R13 cores operating at a base speed of 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, the instance is equipped with a fractional NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU delivering 3 GB of VRAM. Storage is supported by a bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor achieves strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and overall Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also place in the bottom 25%, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-intensive operations. Cryptographic performance remains moderate, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the middle 50%, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets.

The fractional NVIDIA L4 GPU enables entry-level graphics and machine learning capabilities. In LLM inference benchmarks, the instance achieves average prompt processing speeds of 1067.94 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 69.2 tokens per second for a medium 7B model. However, text generation speeds are poor, falling into the bottom 10% with 41.48 tokens per second and 6.21 tokens per second for the respective models. This resource profile offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a dedicated full GPU, though it presents clear tradeoffs in multi-threaded CPU scaling and memory throughput. Appropriate workloads include lightweight graphics rendering, small-scale machine learning inference, and general-purpose tasks requiring modest GPU assistance.
description: Amazon Web Services g6f.xlarge is a graphics-intensive virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It includes a fractional NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 3 GB of VRAM and a bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD. While single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% in stress-ng benchmarks, multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%. The fractional GPU provides entry-level acceleration, delivering average prompt processing speeds for small and medium language models, though text generation throughput remains low. This instance represents a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require modest GPU acceleration and strong single-thread performance, such as lightweight graphics processing, basic machine learning inference, and general-purpose applications with moderate resource demands.
